entry.title: Molina, Vidick & Watrous 2012 · Theorem 2
entry.subtitle: P01 · arXiv v1 (2012-02-17); only arXiv version
entry.summary: Theorem 2. For the classical-verification analogue of Wiesner's quantum money scheme, the optimal simple counterfeiting attack has success probability exactly (3/4 + sqrt(2)/8)^n, for n being the number of qubits in each bank note.
entry.anchor: Theorem 2, p.3; game Sec. 4.1 eq.(8) p.13; Lemma 5 and proof p.14; matching lower bound Lemma 6 p.15

fields.label: Statement verbatim
fields.text: Theorem 2. For the classical-verification analogue of Wiesner's quantum money scheme, the optimal simple counterfeiting attack has success probability exactly (3/4 + sqrt(2)/8)^n, for n being the number of qubits in each bank note.

fields.label: General form lemma5
fields.text: Lemma 5 (p.14): for the n-qudit classical-verification scheme with two bases {e^0_t},{e^1_t} of C^d, success probability <= (3/4 + sqrt(c)/4)^n where c = max_{s,t} |<e^0_s|e^1_t>|^2 (effective overlap; c >= 1/d, footnote 9). Achievable when d = 2. For d = 2 MUB c = 1/2 gives 3/4 + 1/(4 sqrt 2) = 3/4 + sqrt2/8. Qudit Fourier scheme: (3/4 + 1/(4 sqrt d))^n (Lemma 6, tight).

fields.label: Variables
fields.text:
n: number of qubits per ticket
c: effective overlap max_{s,t}|<e^0_s|e^1_t>|^2 (Lemma 5)
d: local dimension (d=2 for Wiesner)

fields.label: Game definition
fields.text: Ticket = Wiesner-type state with secret key k and serial number. Honest verification: user announces serial, bank sends uniformly random challenge c in {0,1}^n (C = {0,1} per qubit); user measures qubit i in the computational basis if c_i=0 and in the Hadamard basis if c_i=1 and reports outcomes; bank accepts iff every position where c_i equals the encoding basis has the correct outcome. Valid single-qubit answers: a = t if b = c, any a if b != c (Sec. 4.2). Simple counterfeiting attack: from ONE ticket, answer TWO independent uniformly random challenges c1, c2 correctly. Attack is modelled as POVMs A^{c1 c2} that depend on BOTH challenges (eq. 8, p.13). Verification destroys the ticket (footnote 6).

fields.label: Assumptions
items: ideal states; exact verification of matching-basis positions
the counterfeiter sees both challenges before measuring (as modelled in eq. 8)

fields.label: Quantifier over adversaries
fields.text: all POVMs on the ticket conditioned on (c1, c2)

fields.label: Not valid for
items: S1: Kent et al. ideal S-token bound is (1/2 + 1/(2 sqrt2))^N, a different game and value
